scope: Rules about another country's system that several sections cite (EU VAT for UK and US freelancers, US forms for French, British and Canadian freelancers) and rules of the domain name registries. The build merges these values into every country's rules; a key may not exist in both.

eu_non_union_scheme.value: A business not established in the EU that supplies services to consumers in the EU can register for the non-Union scheme in one Member State and declare all its EU supplies there: one return per calendar quarter, due by the end of the following month (a nil return when there were no sales); records kept for 10 years.
eu_non_union_scheme.label: EU One Stop Shop, non-Union scheme (suppliers not established in the EU)
eu_non_union_scheme.source_title: The One Stop Shop - VAT e-Commerce - European Commission
eu_non_union_scheme.note: Read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts of the Commission's OSS pages and guidelines. The records must include the information used to determine where the customer is established or usually resides; the older 'two pieces of non-contradictory evidence' presumption (2015 guide) is not shown on the site.

place_of_supply_services_b2b.label: UK VAT: place of supply of services to a business customer (general rule)
place_of_supply_services_b2b.source_title: Place of supply of services (VAT Notice 741A) - GOV.UK
place_of_supply_services_b2b.note: Notice 741A paragraph 6.3, read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts. Special rules (land and property, admission to events, passenger transport, hire of means of transport, restaurant and catering, and for non-business customers cultural, educational and entertainment services, taxed where performed) are checked first. A service to a business customer belonging outside the UK is therefore outside the scope of UK VAT; the customer accounts for any VAT in its own country (reverse charge). A customer who gives a VAT number may be presumed to be in business unless the service is wholly for private use. A business belongs where it has its business establishment or a fixed establishment (the one most directly concerned with the supply when there are several); a private person, where they usually live (VAT Act 1994 section 9, not re-read).

place_of_supply_services_b2c.label: UK VAT: place of supply of services to a non-business customer (general rule)
place_of_supply_services_b2c.source_title: Place of supply of services (VAT Notice 741A) - GOV.UK
place_of_supply_services_b2c.note: Notice 741A paragraph 6.2, read on 2026-10-21 through search excerpts. Non-business customers include private individuals and persons receiving services wholly for a private purpose. Exceptions: special rules, Schedule 4A paragraph 16 services to customers outside the UK, digital services.

eu_b2b_reverse_charge.value: A service supplied to a business customer in the EU is taxed where the customer is established. When the supplier is based outside the EU, the business customer usually accounts for the VAT itself in its own country (reverse charge), and the supplier has no EU VAT to charge.
eu_b2b_reverse_charge.label: EU VAT on services to an EU business customer from a supplier outside the EU (general rule, reverse charge)
eu_b2b_reverse_charge.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of Your Europe and of the Commission page 'Place of taxation' (VAT Directive art. 44: B2B services taxed where the customer is established; art. 196: customer liable). The reverse charge on services from non-established suppliers is applied differently across Member States (art. 194 is optional, some require the customer to be established): the site gives the general rule only. Exceptions (land, events, passenger transport) follow special rules. A valid VAT number is the usual evidence of business status.

eu_b2c_general_rule.value: A service supplied to a private customer is generally taxed where the supplier is established (VAT Directive, art. 45). Exceptions: electronically supplied services are taxed where the customer lives, services connected with land, events and transport follow special rules, and Member States may tax some services used and enjoyed in their territory (art. 59a).
eu_b2c_general_rule.label: EU VAT on services to private customers: general rule and main exceptions
eu_b2c_general_rule.source_title: Place of taxation - Taxation and Customs Union - European Commission
eu_b2c_general_rule.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of the Commission page and of the consolidated VAT Directive (art. 45, 58, 59a). For a supplier established only outside the EU, the general rule places the supply outside the EU: this is the site's reading of art. 45 (not stated in so many words by the sources), hence a cautious answer on the site.

uk_b2b_reverse_charge_overseas.value: A UK business that receives services from a supplier belonging outside the UK accounts for the UK VAT itself (reverse charge) on almost all business-to-business services; the overseas supplier charges no UK VAT.
uk_b2b_reverse_charge_overseas.label: UK reverse charge on services received from overseas suppliers
uk_b2b_reverse_charge_overseas.source_title: Place of supply of services (VAT Notice 741A) - GOV.UK
uk_b2b_reverse_charge_overseas.note: Notice 741A section 5, read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts: the reverse charge applies even if the overseas supplier has a UK VAT registration number; the customer enters output and input tax on its VAT Return (boxes 1, 4, 6 and 7).

uk_netp_no_threshold.value: A business with no establishment in the UK (non-established taxable person) has no VAT registration threshold: it must register as soon as it makes any taxable supply in the UK, including digital services to UK consumers, and notify HMRC within 30 days.
uk_netp_no_threshold.label: UK VAT registration for overseas businesses (no threshold)
uk_netp_no_threshold.source_title: Who should register for VAT (VAT Notice 700/1) - GOV.UK
uk_netp_no_threshold.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of Notice 700/1, HMRC manual VATREG37370 and 'VAT rules for supplies of digital services to consumers' (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-vat-rules-if-you-supply-digital-services-to-private-consumers): threshold not available to NETPs since 1 December 2012; digital services to UK consumers are supplied where the consumer is; without the customer's VAT number, treat the sale as business-to-consumer.

ca_b2b_nonresident.value: A non-resident who does not carry on business in Canada and is not registered generally does not charge the GST/HST on services to a Canadian business that gives its normal GST/HST registration number; the customer self-assesses the tax when it doesn't use the service exclusively in its commercial activities.
ca_b2b_nonresident.label: GST/HST on services from a non-resident to a Canadian business customer
ca_b2b_nonresident.source_title: Doing Business in Canada - GST/HST Information for Non-Residents (RC4027) - Canada.ca
ca_b2b_nonresident.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of RC4027 and GST 300-9 (imported taxable supplies: line 405 of the customer's return, or form GST59 if not registered; 'exclusively' means 90% or more). A customer who doesn't give evidence of its normal registration is a 'specified Canadian recipient' (rule ca_simplified_regime).

ca_simplified_regime.label: Simplified GST/HST registration for non-resident vendors selling services to Canadian consumers
ca_simplified_regime.source_title: Cross-border digital products and services threshold amounts - Canada.ca
ca_simplified_regime.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of the CRA digital-economy pages: a non-resident vendor not carrying on business in Canada and not registered under the normal regime must register under the simplified regime when its taxable supplies of intangible personal property or services to 'specified Canadian recipients' (consumers who haven't shown a normal GST/HST registration) exceed $30,000 CAD over any 12-month period; traditional services such as legal and accounting services are covered, not only streaming or apps (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/charge-collect/cross-border.html). Tax at 5% GST or the HST rate of the recipient's province; sales through a registered distribution platform are excluded from the vendor's threshold; registration through the non-resident web form, no security deposit; amounts in Canadian dollars.

w8ben_purpose.value: Form W-8BEN is given by a non-US individual to the US payer or withholding agent that asks for it (not to the IRS), before the payment, to establish foreign status and claim any treaty benefit. Without it, the payer may have to withhold 30% or apply backup withholding. A foreign company uses Form W-8BEN-E instead, and an individual claiming exemption on pay for services performed in the United States uses Form 8233 or W-4.
w8ben_purpose.label: Form W-8BEN: who gives it, to whom, and why
w8ben_purpose.source_title: Instructions for Form W-8BEN (Rev. October 2021) - IRS
w8ben_purpose.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of the instructions (irs.gov not reachable directly). Line 6a: foreign tax identifying number (required in some cases, such as a US financial account with income reported on Form 1042-S; can replace a US TIN for a treaty claim); line 6b: box for residents of countries that don't require a foreign TIN. The site doesn't say which national number to enter (not verified per country).

w8ben_services_outside_us.value: Pay to a nonresident alien for services performed outside the United States is foreign-source income: it is not subject to US withholding and is not reported on Form 1042-S. When the work is done partly in the United States, the part for US work is US-source (apportioned by time).
w8ben_services_outside_us.label: Services performed outside the US by a nonresident: no US withholding
w8ben_services_outside_us.source_title: Publication 515, Withholding of Tax on Nonresident Aliens and Foreign Entities - IRS
w8ben_services_outside_us.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of Pub. 515 (2026) and the IRS page 'Foreign source income - Form 1042-S reporting not required' (https://www.irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/foreign-source-income-form-1042-s-reporting-not-required). The payer may still ask for Form W-8BEN to document foreign status.

w8ben_validity.label: Form W-8BEN: valid until the last day of the third calendar year after signing, unless circumstances change
w8ben_validity.source_title: Instructions for Form W-8BEN (Rev. October 2021) - IRS
w8ben_validity.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts: a form signed on September 30, 2015 remains valid until December 31, 2018 (IRS example); a change in circumstances that makes information incorrect requires a new form (the deadline to give it was not confirmed in this session). Indefinite validity exists in some cases with documentary evidence, not for treaty claims: not covered by the site.

rdap_servers.label: RDAP servers of the domain extensions offered by the domain name search
rdap_servers.source_title: IANA, RDAP Bootstrap Service Registry for the Domain Name Space (dns.json)

more_sources.source_title: RFC 9224, Finding the Authoritative RDAP Service (IETF), section 4

rdap_servers.note: Read on 2026-10-23 by scripts/verifier_rdap.py in GitHub Actions (file published 2026-10-22T23:00:04Z). co.uk uses the entry of the longest matching label, uk (RFC 9224, section 4). Each server answered 200 for a registered name, 404 for a random name and sent Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. .paris and .bzh also answered correctly but are not offered (their registration conditions were not checked). Not in the IANA file on that date: .eu, .us, .io, .co, .me, .be, .ch, .de. Checked again every month by .github/workflows/verifier-rdap.yml.

fx_reference_sources.label: Official reference exchange rates readable from a browser: ECB (daily), HMRC (monthly period rates), Bank of Canada (daily)
fx_reference_sources.source_title: Euro foreign exchange reference rates - European Central Bank

more_sources.source_title: HMRC exchange rates (monthly, average and spot rates) - UK Trade Tariff
Daily exchange rates - Bank of Canada

fx_reference_sources.note: Checked on 30/10/2026 with the « Lire une source officielle » tool, request sent with the site's origin: the three addresses answer with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (ECB data portal CSV, SHA-256 7572091f…8b1b; HMRC monthly CSV for October 2026, 364161eb…a26e, also September 2026 with a month number without leading zero; Bank of Canada Valet JSON, 9fa55713…503e). The 17 other currencies of the list are quoted by the three sources (ECB and Bank of Canada read for all of them the same day). Conventions: ECB = units of currency per 1 euro, published around 16:00 CET each TARGET working day, for information purposes; HMRC = currency units per £1 for a calendar month (columns Country/Territories, Currency, Currency Code, Currency Units per £1, Start date, End date), the next month's file published in advance; Bank of Canada = Canadian dollars per unit of currency, daily average, business days. The ECB daily XML file (eurofxref-daily.xml) has no CORS header and is not used. Checked each month by scripts/verifier_taux.py (GitHub Actions).

rdap_protocol.label: RDAP answers: 200 when the registry has the domain, 404 when it does not, 429 when queries are rate-limited; servers should allow reading from other websites (CORS)
rdap_protocol.source_title: RFC 7480, HTTP Usage in the Registration Data Access Protocol (IETF), sections 4.2, 5.1, 5.3, 5.5 and 5.6

more_sources.source_title: ICANN, Launching RDAP; Sunsetting WHOIS (27 January 2025)

rdap_protocol.note: RFC 7480: a server returns 404 when it has no object for the query (section 5.3), may return 429 when a client exceeds its limits (section 5.5) and should add Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (section 5.6). ICANN: RDAP became the definitive source of gTLD registration data on 28 January 2025, replacing WHOIS. A 404 only says the registry has no such domain: reserved, blocked or premium names may still not be available at the normal price, which only a registrar can confirm.

rdap_status_dropping.label: RDAP statuses of a domain being deleted (it may become available again)
rdap_status_dropping.source_title: IANA, RDAP JSON Values registry (status values)

more_sources.source_title: RFC 8056, EPP and RDAP Status Mapping (IETF)
RFC 3915, Domain Registry Grace Period Mapping for EPP (IETF)

rdap_status_dropping.note: Read through search excerpts on 2026-10-23. redemption period: a delete has been received and the domain can still be restored; pending delete: deletion requested, not yet complete (purge after the redemption period).

domain_fr_eligibility.value: A .fr name can be registered by a natural person residing, or a legal person whose registered office or principal place of business is, in a Member State of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland; the condition applies for the whole life of the name (the administrative contact must meet it too). Afnic does not check requests beforehand; registration goes through an accredited registrar.
domain_fr_eligibility.label: .fr: who can register (Afnic naming policy)
domain_fr_eligibility.note: Read through search excerpts of the Afnic naming policy and FAQ on 2026-10-23, not the full text.

domain_ca_eligibility.value: A .ca registrant must show a connection with Canada in one of the categories of the Canadian Presence Requirements (for example Canadian citizens, permanent residents, corporations under Canadian law, holders of a trademark registered in Canada).
domain_ca_eligibility.label: .ca: Canadian Presence Requirements (CIRA)
domain_ca_eligibility.source_title: CIRA, Canadian Presence Requirements for Registrants

domain_quebec_eligibility.value: A .quebec registrant (natural or legal person) must be able to show a link or reasonable interest with the Quebec community at registration and for the whole life of the name; some geographic, heritage and generic names are reserved.
domain_quebec_eligibility.label: .quebec: who can register (PointQuébec)

domain_uk_address_for_service.value: Any person may register a .uk or .co.uk name; where the registrant's address is not in the United Kingdom, a UK address for service must also be supplied (not a PO box or equivalent).
domain_uk_address_for_service.label: .uk and .co.uk: registrants outside the UK (Nominet rules)

domain_https_only.label: .dev and .app sites only load over HTTPS (extensions on the HSTS preload list); registrars must say so before purchase

domain_registrar_directories.label: Official lists of accredited registrars (Afnic, ICANN, Nominet, CIRA, PointQuébec)

more_sources.source_title: The UK Domain (Nominet), Who do I buy my domain name from?

domain_registrar_directories.note: Pages found on the official sites on 2026-10-23. The registries do not sell names themselves: names are bought from an accredited registrar (or a reseller). The UK Domain says it cannot recommend one registrar over another.
